seoDescription: Master the powerful rhythm guitar parts of Ghost's iconic track, "Square Hammer," with this in-depth lesson. Learn how to tune your guitar down a whole step to D standard (DGCFAD) to match the original recording. This tutorial breaks down every riff, from the signature intro melody to the driving verse and chorus sections. You'll explore the use of palm-muted power chords, intricate transitional phrases, and the subtle variations that give the song its character, including the rhythm section under the guitar solos.

summary:
## Tuning
To play "Square Hammer" correctly, you must tune your guitar down one full step to **D Standard**.

*   6th (E) string -> **D**
*   5th (A) string -> **G**
*   4th (D) string -> **C**
*   3rd (G) string -> **F**
*   2nd (B) string -> **A**
*   1st (E) string -> **D**

## Key Riffs Breakdown

### Intro Riff
This is the song's signature melodic hook. It's played in two different positions by the two guitarists to create a fuller sound.
*   **Position 1:** Starts on the 2nd fret of the D string.
    *   `D string: 2, 4-5 | A string: 3 | D string: 4-5 | A string: 2 | D string: 4-5 | A string: 5`
*   **Position 2:** Starts on the 7th fret of the A string.
    *   `A string: 7, 9-10 | E string: 8 | A string: 9-10 | E string: 7 | A string: 9-10 | E string: 10`

### Verse Riff
This section uses heavily **palm-muted eighth-note power chords** on the A string, creating a driving rhythm.
*   **Chord Progression:** 7th fret -> 3rd fret -> 2nd fret -> 5th fret.
*   There's a rhythmic accent on the 7th fret chord when the riff repeats.

### Chorus Riff
A more dynamic section that moves around the fretboard.
*   **Part 1:** Starts with a Low E (open) power chord followed by a 3rd fret A-string power chord. It features a slide from the 3rd to the 8th fret on the low E string, leading to a melodic phrase on the A and G strings.
*   **Part 2:** Repeats the initial chord movement but transitions differently, using a 3rd fret low E power chord and 5th fret A power chord.
*   **Transition Lick:** A recurring three-note phrase (`5-7 on low E, 5 on A`) connects different parts of the chorus.

> [!TIP]
> A variation in the second chorus repeat involves a more complex melodic run based on the G power chord (3rd fret, low E string).

## Song Structure & Variations

### Verse 2: Clean Arpeggios
An arpeggiated clean guitar part adds texture over the second verse on the recording. It's based on a chord shape at the 9th fret (D string), 11th fret (G string), and 8th fret (B string).

> [!NOTE]
> This part is very low in the mix and the band often omits it when playing live, so learning it is optional.

### Chorus 2 & 3 Variation
The transition lick at the end of the chorus is slightly altered in the later choruses, adding a slide from the 5th to the 7th fret on the low E string for extra emphasis.

### Solo Section Rhythm
*   **Transition Riff:** The riff used to enter and exit the solos is based on the second half of the main intro riff.
*   **Backing Rhythm:** The rhythm guitar part played underneath the solos is the same power chord progression from the verse.

### Outro
The song ends with a simplified version of the chorus progression, concluding with a final power chord hit (2nd fret low E, 5th fret A) and a simple single-note phrase on the low E string: `5-5, 3-3, 2`.

First off, we are tuned down a whole step. So in order to do that, you're going to tune every string on your guitar down a whole step. So your low E string is going to be tuned down to a D, the A string tuned down to a G, D string tuned down to a C, G string tuned down to an F, B string down to an A, and the high E string down to a D. I'm going to write all those notes out in the description for you. 

So as soon as you get in tune, then you can follow along with this lesson and the original recording pretty easily.

## The Signature Intro Riff

All right, so it's got a fun little riff that intros the song. Typically one will play it there. When they play it together, you'll see that in the transitions at the end of the riffs.

So let's take a look here. We're going to start with this second fret on the D, then four-five on the D, then three on the A string, back to four-five on the D, then the two on the A, then four-five on the D again.

Now you can see I'm using these fingerings so I can jump over with the second finger. This, then I just play four-five with the index and ring finger back to the fifth fret there on the A string. Repeat.

## Layering Guitars & Alternate Voicing

So after a couple of times of playing that, you'll start hearing the second guitars come in with the low E string ringing. I'm just going to call it like it's a standard tuned guitar, it's obviously a D string, but and some feedback on there and the riff is played over that a couple more times. And then that guitar comes in with a full rhythm. 

So that's just the low E power chord, then the third fret power chord off the A string, down to the second fret and move it up to the fifth. So you're just going to repeat that three times.

Now, as that first guitarist continues doing this, the second guitarist, after he plays those chords three times, is going to go up and join him with that riff. But if you watch him play it live, he's doing it up here at the seventh fret. So that's the same riff, it's just starting on the seventh fret of the A string. So seven, nine, ten, over to eight on the low E, back to the nine, ten. 

So if you have it in your hands here, it's the exact same thing, just start here at the seventh fret of the A. All right, so, or you can just jump back and play it there. It's really the same notes but they do, the strings sound different, so it kind of fills up the sound having that same riff played on different strings.

## Playing the Verse Riff

All right, so now we get to the actual verse section. It sounds like this.

All right, so that riff, it's just kind of starting on some power chords here on the A string. So, seventh fret power chord, just eighth notes, kind of heavily palm-muted. Down to three, two, back to five. So I do this, and then the first time when you're coming back around to repeat the chords again, hit that first chord. Just, there's a couple of accents there on that power chord. 

So... this, then just continue the riff the exact same... I'm sorry, seven, three, two, then five. So we have seven, three, two, five. And then we start the second time around with... then we go back through the chords the same way as the first time, and end it with that riff. 

All right, then we go back, you know, through the verse again and it just has this little, always has the kind of like that transition riff at the end of it.

## Dissecting the Chorus Riff

All right, then we get to the chorus. Um, it's a fun one, looks like this.

All right, so that kind of moves around quite a bit here. We're going to start with the low E power chord to the third fret power chord off the A string. This, now we're going to do a slide from the third fret of the low E up to the eighth, to the 10th fret on the A, to the seventh on the G. Then we have the power chord there at the G string, third, then the fifth, and then we have this little transition that's 5-7 on the low E and 5 on the A. So we have this so far. Then kind of repeat the same thing except you don't do that little slide, you just have the third power chord over to the third fret of the low E, up to the fifth fret there of the A string, and then that little three-note riff again. So 5-7 of the low E to 5 on the A. So I'm just going to go through that real slowly so you can just watch me play all that. So it's kind of one time through the chorus.

So when you repeat the chorus, starts the same way, same exact thing. So there's a little different ending there. So that little thing, it's based off the G power chord. And then you're going to go, you hit that G power chord a couple times, then you pick the fifth fret of the A string to the sixth string, third fret. So this, then reach up and grab the seventh fret of the D, back to three on the low E, then to the fifth fret of the D, to the fifth fret of the A. So this... and then that same little three-note riff. Now if you just have another rhythm guitarist not doing it, you can just jump to the chord like normal.

## Verse 2: Clean Guitar Arpeggios

Believe we go back to that little, they always use that kind of riff as a transition. It's going to take us back to verse number two. Now, verse two has a little variation. It's at the 1 minute and 48 second mark. They actually don't do this live so you can leave it. It's pretty low in the mix if you don't want to do it, but I'm going to teach it just kind of for completeness sake here. There's a little clean guitar part, sounds like this. So kind of a way of just adding a little creepy vibe to the verse there.

## Chorus 2 & 3 Variation

All right so what else do we have here? We have on the chorus two, there's a little variation when we go around to repeat. And they do that in both the second and third chorus.

## Solo Section: Transitions & Rhythm

All right, so now all we have to really cover are the stuff that goes on during the guitar solo and the ending of the song. So we have right here, the solo kind of has a different way they transition into the solos, and they use that same transition leaving the solos. Like this.

All right, so that's just the open A string, then you're going to hit it with four eighth notes. Then go 2-3 on the A. Just use your index finger for both of them, because then you're going to play 4-5 on the D string over to five on the A. And it's just like the same, the same as the main riff. This, it's the same as the main riff, the second half of it there, right?

And then leaving the solo at the very end of the second solo... then that takes you back into the chorus. Now, so that was the same thing that we went into the solos with.

## Song Outro and Conclusion

Now at the very end of the song, they play the chords just kind of straight through and have a little different ending at the very, very end of the song.

All right, so that is just going for the low E and then the power chord off the third fret of the A, then the third fret off the low E, and then the fifth fret of the A. So very similar, just kind of, it's like the chorus with no frills. But the very last time you're playing it, they'll just play the same thing but instead of going to the D here, they do that, which is the second fret of the low E and the fifth fret there of the A string. 

And then we have at least one guitar player just plays single notes, which is the fifth fret there on the low E a couple times, then a couple times on the three, then once on the two. The other one may play just power chords of that. And then the music's gone. 

All right, so stay tuned for the next one. We're going to take a look at both of the guitar solos. They're really fun to play, and you'll see it tomorrow.
